Hi Elena — great to hear the demo was useful, and thanks for sending over the sec questionnaire. Below is a short recap and recommended path tailored to Clearslate's signals. I copied Ben (AE) and Priyom (Solutions Eng) so they have visibility for procurement and the sandbox setup.

Recap of options (short):
- Hosted API (fastest path): ideal for a 2-week pilot. Provides managed keys, streaming, and Redwood-managed runtime. We can enable contract-level controls (DPA, SOC references) and restrict ingress/egress to your VPC via egress peering where needed. Most customers with PHI evaluate Hosted first if contractual terms + VPC egress meet their security bar; otherwise they move to Private for full customer-controlled networking.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed throughput — good when you need predictable steady tps and guaranteed burst headroom. If you must guarantee 120+ tps during business hours, Dedicated is the safer bet for production, but for a pilot Hosted usually suffices with burst policies.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full isolation and customer-managed networking/KMS. Recommended when regulatory constraints require customer-controlled keys or when the data cannot leave customer-controlled networks. Longer lead time.

Hosted evaluation quickstart (recommended for pilot):
1) Sandbox endpoints: we'll provision a sandbox namespace for Clearslate: https://sandbox.redwood.host/clearslate-eval (read-only demo tokens for the first week).
2) Rate caps: default sandbox caps are 60 requests/sec per endpoint; we can request a temporary raise to 150 rps for the pilot window (2 weeks) subject to approval.
3) Prefix/KV cache: enable prefix caching on the chat endpoint to reduce token costs during repeated prompts — reduces latency for repeated context.
4) Token provisioning & telemetry: Priyom will create an initial API key scoped to the sandbox and wire up the cost/latency dashboards for your team.
5) Security artifacts: we will return the filled security questionnaire and attach SOC2 summary + DPA (Ben will handle contracting touches).

Suggested next steps (action items):
- Elena / Clearslate: confirm PHI scope for the pilot (which endpoints will ingest PHI) by EOD Wed (2029-05-22). (Elena)
- Redwood: provision sandbox namespace, create scoped API key, and review the questionnaire — expected completion Tue (Priyom + Hannah)
- Procurement: Ben to send standard pilot agreement and SOC2 artifacts once questionnaire scope confirmed (Ben)
- Follow-up call: 30 min on Thu 2029-05-23 to confirm sandbox access and rate raise plan (all)

Notes on Hosted vs Dedicated for Clearslate signal: if your CISO requires customer KMS + no Redwood-managed keys for pilot data, lean Private. If procurement's ask is only to see SOC2/DPA and to restrict egress, Hosted + VPC egress should be acceptable and is the faster path. For production throughput guarantees at 120 tps, we can design a Dedicated commit conversation during the pilot.

Attachments referenced: we will add a Redwood quickstart checklist (pdf) and the completed sec questionnaire back to you.

I'll have Priyom post the sandbox credentials into the shared Drive link and Ben will start the procurement thread.

Thanks — talk soon,
Hannah
